quest.title: Soheil's Wish
quest.description: Soheil's archaeological notes record his desert adventures in his youth. Some of the ruins mentioned may contain treasures and old records. Head into the depths of the desert again to look for them.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x100, Primogem x20, Mora x10000

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Phew, it's a lot cooler here. Mind letting me see the slate?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Soheil examines the slate, alternating between frowning and marveling.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you're spending too much time on this! You're not trying to commit the text to memory and skimp on our pay, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Sorry, I was just so fascinated. This is my first time seeing writing like this...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Any discoveries?

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Hmm... Some of it looks like a construction log... It mentions "Aaru," but there's no way to know if it's in any way connected to Aaru Village. Too bad the records say little more...

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: But this discovery is certainly worth several pages of writing. Thank you very much. Here, as per our agreement.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: My next step would be to find a bigger collection of primary materials, but that's going to be difficult without going into the desert...

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Oh, I have an idea! If you have the time, please hear me out...

response.speaker: Hulwani
response.text: Mr. Soheil, are you thinking...

response.speaker: Hulwani
response.text: The sage prohibits any researcher from going into the desert.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Now, I wouldn't dare challenge the sage's authority, but I'm sure he never prohibited the giving of gifts, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gifts? What are you going to give us?

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Something very precious... My archaeology notes.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: To be honest, I ventured into the desert more than a dozen years ago, but didn't find anything special other than noting the locations of several potential ruins.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: I believe it's fate that brought me back here to make your acquaintance in these ruins, so I want you to have these notes!

response.speaker: Hulwani
response.text: Are you trying to... I get it. That isn't against the rules, but I'm afraid your actions would...

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: #My actions? I am simply presenting a gift as a celebration of my friendship with {NICKNAME} the big hero and Paimon the little hero. Isn't that more than fair?

response.speaker: Hulwani
response.text: I suppose...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The world of researchers is way too complicated! He could just have come right out and said he needed our help! Instead, we had to go through this whole charade...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you ask Paimon, he's just afraid that the big guy over there would rat him out to the sage.

choices.text: It's because your world is too simple, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is it? Paimon thinks her world's pretty complicated. Paimon has to remember what every dish tastes like, and all the ways to get different treasures...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's take a look at what's written in Soheil's gift!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm... Looks like he's been having a pretty hard time. He explored the area around the Mausoleum of King Deshret for a month without obtaining any results. He didn't want to give up, and found the Transparent Ruins.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And then he found something a lot smaller than the Mausoleum of King Deshret — the Tomb of Carouses. Finally, he was attacked by a group of mercenaries in a place called Lamb-Devourer Rock.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa... Even though he went through all that, he still wrote that "compared to the mockery, having no improvement in knowledge is more painful to endure."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He sounded like a completely different person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Seems like he really was in it for the knowledge back then. Paimon's a little moved.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From that perspective, it wouldn't be an exaggeration for him to call this a precious gift.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's visit each location mentioned in his notes. If we find something decent, let's bring it back as a gift to him in return!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course! He was just short of writing "Help me!" all over his face! Hmm, if we help him now, I'm sure we'll get loads of rewards.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True, but Paimon feels these researchers always hide behind the pretense of "pursuing knowledge"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As if that justifies everything they do and say.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, that's one thing you shouldn't turn into, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, Paimon's never been interested in knowledge at all!

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Oh... Is it not enough? Well, consider it as a greeting gift. I'll have better ones for you later!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks it's pretty fair...

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Well, the little hero certainly thinks so. What does the big hero think?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay...

choices.text: You should be thanking Tirzad instead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! If we weren't trying to prove Tirzad correct, we wouldn't have found this slate!

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: You're right. Tirzad's the one I should be thanking — yes, indeed!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We explored the Tomb of Carouses.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: So you went to the Tomb of Carouses... It's a miniature version of the Mausoleum of King Deshret, just like I said, right? So, any new discoveries?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You recount your exploration of the Tomb of Carouses to Soheil and give him the stone slate.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: It sounds like you didn't find anything special. I guess size isn't the only difference between the two locations.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: And as for this slate...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it, what is it? It has so many words, so it's got to be valuable, right?

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: From what I can tell, it's an ordinary fable that features some animals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? How can this be?

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: But that's okay, I can still squeeze a paper out of this, albeit a short one...

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: "The Retreat of the Sheep: A Preliminary Study of Environmental Change in the Desert."

talks.objective: Go deeper into the desert and explore according to Soheil's archaeology notes

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We explored the Transparent Ruins.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: You went to the Transparent Ruins? Did you find anything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course. Be prepared to be thunderstruck!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You recount your exploration of the Transparent Ruins to Soheil and give him the three stone slates.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Aha! So King Deshret did indeed withhold a secret behind that unknown force. I shall get to the bottom of it.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: This is...

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: How could this be...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you look pale... Did you discover something terrible?

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Uh... No, sorry, they're not exactly "terrible"... The writings on the stone slates look complicated, but they're actually... Records of leave requests.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: In addition, the recorded excuses are not any different from that of the young scholars today...

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Phew, it's a good thing I failed to find a way to access the Transparent Ruins back in the day. I imagine that I would have been quite livid.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Anyway, I must thank you for bringing the slates back. Perhaps I should go ask around about the excuses people make in Mondstadt. That could be enough for me to write a paper...

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: "Time Out From a Busy Schedule: On the Evolution of the Perception of Off-Days in Different Societies."

talks.objective: Go deeper into the desert and explore according to Soheil's archaeology notes

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We explored the Lamb-Devourer Rock.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: You weren't in any danger, were you? Not that I doubt you could handle any situation, even if you did encounter Thutmose.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You recount your exploration of Lamb-Devourer Rock to Soheil and give him the stone slate.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: So there is a secret base after all... No wonder Thutmose still managed to rob me despite all the precautions I took.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: What a bunch of ignorant fools! They claim to worship King Deshret, and yet they randomly throw such important relics around! Inexcusable!

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: I must thank you on behalf of the Akademiya for getting such a valuable... Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? What's with the sudden frown? Did you run into something difficult to decipher?

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Just the opposite, really. It's a love poem.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Perhaps this slate would be more valuable to those from Haravatat. I can already imagine what titles they'll come up with...

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: "On the Relationship Between the Development of Rhetoric and the Progress of Civilization."

talks.objective: Go deeper into the desert and explore according to Soheil's archaeology notes

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Now that the three ruins have been fully explored, I can finally put my thoughts to rest.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Well then, to celebrate the strengthening of our friendship, I shall prepare more gifts of gratitude for our big hero and little hero.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's nothing, really! Plus, we found lots of treasure based on your notes! So, how's your paper going?

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: The papers... Yeah, even though I've collected enough materials, I no longer depend on churning out volumes.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: It's a breakthrough I'm after... I must still go into the Mausoleum of King Deshret myself.

response.speaker: Hulwani
response.text: But the sage said...

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Yes, I get it, it's always about the sage with you... I'm just griping, that's all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What do you need a breakthrough for?

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: To become a candidate for the next sage, of course.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: To outsiders, the difference between a researcher and a sage is that of a small fruit and a larger fruit.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: In reality, the gap is even greater than the difference between a hilichurl and slime.

choices.text: Those are two completely different things.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: That's exactly it. They are two different things altogether.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: The sages, with the power they control, virtually have all of us researchers by our throats. They could make or break us with just one word.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: So many people have labored and fought over papers, some even as old as me. We'd give up our dignity just for a chance to be deemed worthy by the sages.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Therefore, I must become a sage myself, or all the suffering I've endured would've been for nothing. I'm sure you'd understand if you were a researcher!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No, Paimon thinks {NICKNAME} would be more like the you in the notes.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Notes?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Remember what you wrote in your notes? "Compared to the mockery, having no improvement in knowledge is more painful to endure."

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: What? I wrote that?

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Hmm... The experiences I've had are indeed true. But if it weren't for your reminder, I would have never looked at things from that perspective again.

choices.text: So you've forgotten all about it...

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: #...{NICKNAME}, Paimon. This is a bit abrupt, but there's one more favor I'd like to ask.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Do you want us to look for more stone slates?

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: No no no, I have enough stone slates... I just... feel like reading my old notes again.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Please allow me to take back the archaeology notes I gave you. I'll prepare something else as a gift for you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Thank you for all your help, and may your travels be smooth.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: Also, thanks for reminding me of a time when I was younger. It's a pretty good feeling.

choices.text: It's good to remember everything again.

response.speaker: Soheil
response.text: The difference is that they're completely different.

choices.text: You scratch our back, we scratch yours.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We got treasure and you got inspiration for your papers.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: You're back. Did you find anything special in the desert?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not yet.

dialogues.speaker: Soheil
dialogues.text: Alright. If you do find anything, please share them with me and quench my thirst for knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Hulwani
dialogues.text: Since the sage didn't specifically ban travelers from entering the desert... Yes, you may go ahead...
